title: dual_track.py – Dual‑Track Documentation Generator

concept.big_picture: `dual_track.py` turns source code or change logs into two separate explanations: one for programmers and one for non‑technical readers. It does all work offline and can be run from any project.
concept.data_and_privacy: The tool never sends data over the network; all processing happens locally. No personal data is transmitted.
concept.worst_case: If the tool is run on a corrupted or incomplete source, the output may be incomplete but it will still produce a Markdown file. No system crashes occur.

real_world_impact.battery_cpu_ram: Minimal CPU usage – a few milliseconds per file. Memory consumption is proportional to file size; it stays below 10 MB for typical projects.
real_world_impact.speed: On a modest laptop it takes less than a second to generate documentation for a single file.
real_world_impact.your_privacy: No data leaves your machine; the tool reads files locally.

kill_switch_explained.what_it_is: The kill switch is the `--no-validate` flag which skips quality validation.
kill_switch_explained.without_it: Without it, the command validates automatically, ensuring the output meets quality thresholds.
kill_switch_explained.real_life_analogy: Think of it as a safety lock on a car: normally locked, but you can turn it off to speed up the start.

open_source_angle: The project uses a permissive license, allowing anyone to use, modify, and distribute the code.
should_you_run_this: If you need consistent, dual‑track documentation generated automatically, run the tool from the project root. It works offline.
why_it_matters: Consistent documentation reduces maintenance effort and aligns technical and non‑technical audiences.

claim_sources.claim: The script runs offline and does not contact external services.
claim_sources.evidence: Embedded comment: "This script never makes a network call."
